key_insight: AI/ML is transforming chemical engineering by augmenting first-principles models across scales, from atoms and materials to process operations, with physics-informed hybrids emerging as the dominant direction.
engineering_relevance: For chemical engineers, these methods improve prediction, design, and control when data are sparse, systems are complex, and reliability matters.
method: Embed physics constraints such as conservation laws and thermodynamic consistency
Use AI/ML across multiscale tasks including discovery, transport, separations, and operations
evidence_signal: The paper is a perspective that synthesizes recent methodological developments and representative applications across multiple chemical engineering domains rather than reporting a single new dataset or benchmark.
watch_item: Black-box models can struggle with extrapolation, interpretability, and lifecycle management, so deployment requires careful validation and domain-aware constraints.
paper_title: Atoms to Processes: The Role of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Chemical Engineering
